newsitem.title: USA: Protest at NYSE over NationsBank merger.
newsitem.headline: Protest at NYSE over NationsBank merger.

text.p: About 100 protestors opposing NationBank Corp's acquisition of Boatmen's Bancshares Inc picketed outside the New York Stock Exchange Friday morning.
No arrests or injuries were reported, according to police.
The protestors, which included minority contractors from St. Louis and New York, seek to halt the merger and say they have filed a complaint with the U.S. Federal Reserve Board.
"We have filed a complaint with the Federal Reserve and we want to stop this merger," said Eddie Hassan of the St. Louis Minority Contractors.
"We are concerned what Boatman's lending practices will be after the merger."
He said the group has appealed to NationsBank to adopt commitments to minority businesses before the merger is sealed, including $1 billion in loans to minority businesses.
Another New York-based coalition of community groups filed a challenge to the merger with the Federal Reserve in October.
A NationsBank spokeswoman said it has already outlined a community investment and lending plan for the St. Louis area and does not forsee the group's action jeopardizing the merger.
"(NationsBank is) a proven leader in community lending, and our goal is to be the premier community development parner in the markets where we do business," Melba Spencer said.
